λόγῳ ἐπέπληξα, ἵνα διδαχθῶσιν οἱ διὰ τούτου ἐπανορθούμενοι ἑαυτοὺς καὶ
ἐλεγχθῶσιν οἱ μὴ ὑπακούοντες λόγῳ, χρῄζοντες δὲ τῆς διὰ τῶν πραγμάτων
ἀποτομίας. 295,ξολ2 Εἰδὼς ὅτι καὶ ἀκούοντές τινες πείθονται, οὐ βούλομαι ἤδη
ἀπο296,ξολ2 τομίᾳ χρήσασθαι, ἀλλ' ὅταν ὑπακούοντες φανῶσιν, ἵνα δειχθῶσιν,
τίνες οἱ λόγῳ παιδευόμενοι καὶ τίνες οἱ ἐπιστροφίας δεόμενοι. 2 Kor 10,7 Ἕκαστον
ἀκριβῶς δοκιμάζετε τὸ κατ' ἀξίαν τῆς ἀναστροφῆς τοῦ προσώπου. τοῦτο δὲ ὁρᾷ εἰς
τοὺς ἀποστόλους· ἐπειδὴ γὰρ ἔμελλεν ἐλέγχειν τοὺς ἐκ περιτομῆς, ἐκεῖνοι δὲ
προεβάλλοντο Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην, ἀσφαλίσασθε, φησί, μή ποτε τὸ
ἀξίωμα τῶν προσώπων μὴ ἐάσῃ ὑμᾶς τὸ ἀληθὲς συνιδεῖν. 2 Kor 10,12 Ταῦτα
γράφομεν οὐ μιμούμενοι τοὺς συνιστῶντας ἑαυτούς– οὐ γὰρ καλὸν τοῦτο–· οὐ γὰρ
νοοῦσιν ὅτι αὐτοὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς αὐτοὺς μετροῦσιν καὶ οὐκ ἄλλῳ δύνανται
παρατίθεσθαι· ἄλλοις γὰρ συγκρινόμενοι οὐδέν εἰσιν. 2 Kor 10,14 Οὐχ ὡς εὐτελεῖς
ἐπὶ μείζοσι καυχώμεθα ὑπὲρ τὸ ἑαυτῶν μέτρον· καὶ γὰρ ἕως ὑμῶν ἤλθομεν καὶ
ἐκηρύξαμεν τὸν λόγον. 2 Kor 10,15–16 Ἐκεῖνοι τοῖς ἡμετέροις καυχῶνται καμάτοις,
ἡμεῖς δὲ οὔ, ἀλλὰ κατὰ νόμον τὸν κανόνα καὶ τὸ μερισθὲν ἡμῖν μέτρον καυχώμεθα,
ἐλπίζοντες αὐξηθείσης τῆς ὑμετέρας πίστεως καὶ ἐπέκεινα ὑμῶν εὐαγγελίσασθαι.
κανόνα δὲ λέγει τὸ μέχρις αὐτῶν τέως ἀφικέσθαι. 2 Kor 10,17 Εἰ καὶ καυχώμεθα,
ἀλλ' οὐχ ὡς συνέσει οἰκείᾳ κατορθοῦντες ἀλλὰ τῇ χάριτι τοῦ πνεύματος. 2 Kor 11,2
Ἀπεθάνετε, φησί, τῷ νόμῳ, ἑτέρῳ ἀνδρὶ γεγόνατε, τῷ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστάντι. πῶς οὖν
παρθένος ἁγνὴ πρότερον γαμουμένη; ἀλλὰ 297 διὰ λουτροῦ παλιγγενεσίας
ἀναγεννηθεῖσα καὶ εἰς ἕτερον βίον μετελθοῦσα, παρθένος ἁγνὴ δικαίως ὠνόμασται.
2 Kor 11,4 Τὸν Χριστιανισμὸν βεβαιοῖ ἡ εἰς Χριστὸν πίστις καὶ ἡ τοῦ πνεύματος
ἔλλαμψις. εἰ τοίνυν ταῦτα παρ' ὑμῶν μὴ ἐλάβετε, καλῶς ἐζητεῖτε τοὺς ἔτι κατὰ
νόμον ζῆν βουλομένους. 2 Kor 11,10–12 Οὐ Korινθίους ὀνειδίζων τοῦτό φησιν, ἀλλὰ
τοὺς ὡς ἐμπορίᾳ χρωμένους τῷ κηρύγματι ἐλέγχει. διό φησιν ὅτι οὐ παύομαι
καυχώμενος, ὅτι οὐ πεποίηκα ἐμπορίαν τὸ κήρυγμα ὡς ἐκεῖνοι· οὐδὲ γὰρ ἔλαβόν τι
παρ' ὑμῶν οὐδὲ λαμβάνω, οὐχ ὡς μὴ ἀγαπῶν ὑμᾶς– ἀγαπῶ γάρ–ἀλλ' ἵνα τῶν
κατηγόρων ἐκκόψω τὴν πρόφασιν, ἵνα εἴτε ψευδῶς εἴτε ἀληθῶς καυχῶνται,
φανερωθῶσιν ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς πεφανερώμεθα. 2 Kor 12,2–5 Τοῦτο ἰσχυρὸν δεῖξαι
ψυχὴν ἀθάνατον· εἰ γὰρ ᾔδει ὅτι θνητὴ ἦν, οὐκ ἂν ἀμφέβαλλεν, πότερον τὴν
ὀπτασίαν ἐκτὸς σώματος εἶδεν ἢ ἐν σώματι. τὸ δὲ ἕως τρίτου οὐρανοῦ τοῦ
διαστήματος ἔφη τὸ τρίτον· εἰ γὰρ ἦν ἕως τριῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνελθών, πάντως ἂν ἐκεῖ
τὰ ἄρρητα ῥήματα ἤκουσεν καὶ οὐκ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ. καὶ μηδεὶς οἰέσθω τὸν
παράδεισον εἶναι ὑπὲρ τὸν οὐρανόν· κατὰ γὰρ ἀνατολὰς πεφύτευται ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐν
τῷ τόπῳ τῷ Ἐδέμ, ὅθεν καὶ ὁ Ἀδὰμ ἐπλάσθη ὡς Μωϋσῆς ἱστορεῖ. ἀσθενείας δέ φησι
τοὺς διωγμούς, οὐ σωματικὸν πάθος ὡς οἴονταί τινες. 2 Kor 12,7 Ὑποπτεύεται παρὰ
πολλῶν ὡς ἄλγημα ἔχων περὶ τὴν κεφαλήν, τὸ δὲ ἀληθὲς τοὺς διωγμοὺς λέγει,
ἐπειδὴ ἀπὸ διαβολικῆς ἐνεργείας ἐγίνοντο οἱ πειρασμοί. τὸν δὲ πειρασμὸν
ὑπηρετούμενον τῷ διαβόλῳ ἄγγελον σατᾶν προσηγόρευσεν ἀπὸ μεταφορᾶς τῶν
ἀγγέλων τῶν ὑπηρετουμένων θεῷ. τὸ δὲ ἐδόθη κατὰ συγχώρησιν θεοῦ νοητέον ὡς
καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ Ἰώβ· οὐ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς δίδωσι κακά. 298 2 Kor 12,9 Ἔχεις χάριν ἀποστολικήν,
μὴ ζήτει ταύτην καὶ ἄνευ πειρασμῶν κατορθοῦν· ἡ γὰρ δύναμίς μου τελειοῦται ἐν
διωγμοῖς καὶ θλίψεσιν. 2 Kor 12,13 Εἰ μὴ ἄρα μοι τοῦτο ἔχετε ἐγκαλεῖν, ὅτι οὐκ
ἔλαβόν τι παρ' ὑμῶν εἰς διατροφὴν ἀποναρκήσας πρὸς τὴν ἔνδειαν, ἐν ᾧ εἰ καὶ
ἡμαρτηκέναι με νομίζετε, σύγγνωτέ μοι καὶ χαρίσασθέ μοι τὴν ἀδικίαν ταύτην ἣν
ἠδικεῖσθαι παρ' ἐμοῦ νομίζετε. 2 Kor 12,14 Τοῦτο μαρτύρεται αὐτοὺς πρὸς τὸ
δεύτερον καὶ τρίτον γενέσθαι πρὸς αὐτοὺς διὰ τὸ κήρυγμα. 2 Kor 13,4 Ὥσπερ ὁ
Χριστὸς εἴρηται ἁμαρτία καὶ κατάρα γεγονέναι, οὔτε ἁμαρτία ὢν οὔτε κατάρα, ἀλλὰ
τὰ ἡμέτερα κακὰ ἰδιοποιήσατο, ἵνα ἡμᾶς ἀπ' αὐτῶν ἐξέληται· οὕτω καὶ νῦν ἐξ
ἀσθενείας οὐ τῆς ἑαυτοῦ λέγεται ἐσταυρῶσθαι, ἀλλ' ἧς ἀνεδέξατο ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, τὰ
ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν οἰκονομῶν.
pass_a_gloss:
[Continues the 10:2-6 note: "but first] I rebuked by word, so that those correcting themselves through this might be taught, and those not obeying a word, but needing the severity through deeds, might be exposed.
[Second catena form of the same note, marked 295 col. 2 and 296 col. 2: knowing that some are persuaded even by hearing, I do not want to use severity already, but when they appear obeying, so that it may be shown who are those trained by word and who are those needing correction. Every clause has its counterpart in the first form; not printed again.]
[Label 2 Cor 10:7.] Examine each one accurately, the thing according to the worth of the conduct of the person. And this looks to the apostles; for since he was going to refute those of the circumcision, and they were putting forward Peter and James and John, make yourselves safe, he says, lest perhaps the dignity of the persons not allow you to see the truth.
[Label 2 Cor 10:12.] These things we write not imitating those commending themselves (for this is not good); for they do not understand that they measure themselves among themselves and are not able to be set beside another; for compared with others they are nothing.
[Label 2 Cor 10:14.] Not as cheap people do we boast over greater things beyond our own measure; for we did come as far as you and preached the word.
[Label 2 Cor 10:15-16.] Those boast in our labors, but we do not; but according to law we boast the rule and the measure apportioned to us, hoping, your faith having been increased, to preach the gospel even beyond you. And he calls rule the arriving as far as them for the present.
[Label 2 Cor 10:17.] Even if we boast, yet not as succeeding by our own understanding but by the grace of the Spirit.
[Label 2 Cor 11:2.] You died, he says, to the law; you have become another man's, the one who rose from the dead. How then a pure virgin, being married before? But [page number 297 dropped] having been born again through a washing of regeneration and having passed over into another life, she has rightly been named a pure virgin.
[Label 2 Cor 11:4.] Faith in Christ and the illumination of the Spirit confirm Christianity. So if you did not receive these things from you [the Greek has ὑμῶν, read as ἡμῶν, "us"], you were rightly seeking those still wishing to live according to law.
[Label 2 Cor 11:10-12.] Not reproaching Corinthians does he say this, but he refutes those using the preaching as a trade. Therefore he says: I do not stop boasting that I have not made the preaching a trade as those have; for neither did I take anything from you nor do I take, not as not loving you (for I love), but so that I may cut off the pretext of the accusers, so that, whether they boast falsely or truly, they may be made manifest, as we too have been made manifest.
[Label 2 Cor 12:2-5.] This is strong to show the soul immortal; for if he knew that it was mortal, he would not have been in doubt whether he saw the vision outside a body or in a body. And "as far as the third heaven" he said of the third of the distance; for if he had gone up as far as three heavens, he would surely have heard the unspeakable words there and not in the paradise. And let no one suppose the paradise to be above the heaven; for it has been planted toward the east on the earth in the place Eden, from where also Adam was formed, as Moses relates. And he calls the persecutions weaknesses, not a bodily suffering as some think.
[Label 2 Cor 12:7.] He is suspected by many as having a pain about the head, but the truth is he means the persecutions, since the trials came from diabolical working. And the trial serving the devil he called an angel of Satan, by metaphor from the angels serving God. And the "was given" is to be understood according to God's permission, as also in the case of Job; for God does not give evils. [Page number 298 dropped.]
[Label 2 Cor 12:9.] You have apostolic grace; do not seek to accomplish this also without trials; for my power is perfected in persecutions and afflictions.
[Label 2 Cor 12:13.] Unless then you have this to charge me with, that I did not take anything from you for maintenance, having grown numb toward the want; in which, even if you think me to have sinned, pardon me and forgive me this injustice which you think you are wronged by me.
[Label 2 Cor 12:14.] This he testifies to them toward his coming to them a second and a third time on account of the preaching.
[Label 2 Cor 13:4.] Just as Christ is said to have become sin and a curse, being neither sin nor a curse, but he made our evils his own so that he might take us out from them, so also now he is said to have been crucified out of weakness, not his own, but which he took up on our behalf, managing the things on our behalf.
pass_b_english: … I rebuked with a word, so that those who correct themselves by it would be taught, and those who do not obey a word but need the severity of deeds would be exposed.

On 2 Corinthians 10:7: Test each one carefully by what the person's conduct is worth. This looks to the apostles. He was about to refute those of the circumcision, and they kept putting forward Peter, James and John; so he says, Be on your guard, so that the rank of these persons does not keep you from seeing the truth.

On 2 Corinthians 10:12: We write this without imitating those who commend themselves, for that is not good. They do not understand that they measure themselves by themselves and cannot stand comparison with anyone else; set beside others, they are nothing.
On 2 Corinthians 10:14: We are not cheap men boasting of great things beyond our own measure; for we did come as far as you and preached the word.

On 2 Corinthians 10:15–16: They boast of our labors; we do not. We boast, as is right, of the rule and the measure assigned to us, and we hope, as your faith grows, to preach the gospel even beyond you. By “rule” he means that he has come as far as them for the present.
On 2 Corinthians 10:17: Even if we boast, it is not as though we succeed by our own understanding, but by the grace of the Spirit.

On 2 Corinthians 11:2: You died to the law, he says, and you have become another man's, the one who rose from the dead (Romans 7:4). How then can she be a pure virgin, when she was married before? But born again through the washing of regeneration (Titus 3:5), and passed into another life, she is rightly called a pure virgin.

On 2 Corinthians 11:4: Faith in Christ and the illumination of the Spirit confirm Christianity. So if you had not received these from [us], you would be right to look for those who still want to live by the law.

On 2 Corinthians 11:10–12: He says this not to reproach the Corinthians but to expose those who treat the preaching as a trade. That is why he says: I do not stop boasting that I have not made the preaching a trade, as they have; I have taken nothing from you and take nothing now. It is not that I do not love you, for I do; it is to cut away my accusers' pretext, so that, whether their boasting is false or true, they may be shown for what they are, as we have been shown.

On 2 Corinthians 12:2–5: This is strong proof that the soul is immortal; if he had known it to be mortal, he would not have doubted whether he saw the vision out of the body or in the body. By “as far as the third heaven” he meant the third part of the distance; for if he had gone up through three heavens, he would surely have heard the unspeakable words there and not in paradise. And let no one think that paradise lies above heaven: it was planted in the east, on earth, in the place called Eden, from where Adam too was formed, as Moses relates (Genesis 2:8). By “weaknesses” he means the persecutions, not a bodily illness, as some think.

On 2 Corinthians 12:7: Many suspect that he had a pain in his head, but in truth he means the persecutions, since the trials came from the devil's working. He called the trial that serves the devil “an angel of Satan,” by a metaphor from the angels who serve God. “Was given” must be understood as by God's permission, as in the case of Job; for God does not give evil things.
On 2 Corinthians 12:9: You have apostolic grace; do not ask to carry it out free of trials as well, for my power is made perfect in persecutions and afflictions.

On 2 Corinthians 12:13: Unless, then, you have this charge against me: that I took nothing from you for my keep and grew numb to my own want. If you think I sinned in this, pardon me, and forgive me the wrong you think I did you.
On 2 Corinthians 12:14: He calls them to witness this, concerning his coming to them a second and a third time because of the preaching.

On 2 Corinthians 13:4: Christ is said to have become sin and a curse (2 Corinthians 5:21; Galatians 3:13), though he was neither sin nor a curse; he made our evils his own in order to rescue us from them. In the same way he is now said to have been crucified through weakness: not his own, but the weakness he took on for us, as he managed everything for our sake.
notes: 2026-11-11 claude-sumfix-b3: retranslated from the locked Greek. The old English was a word-order gloss and printed wrong references: '(2 Cor 11:10–12)' after the 11:4 note and '(2 Cor 13:4)' after the 12:14 note on the second and third visit. Doublet collapsed: the 295/296 col. 2 second form of the 10:2-6 note (no new material; the first form ends at the top of this section). παρ' ὑμῶν in 11:4 read as 'from [us]'. Labels one per note (10:7 to 13:4); page and column marks dropped; section opens mid-sentence with '…'.

choices.term: second form of the 10:2-6 note (295/296 col. 2)
choices.why: Every clause has a counterpart in the first form, which ends at the top of this section; recorded in translator_notes.
The sentence 'If then you did not receive these things...' is the edition's 11:4 note; the old English printed (2 Cor 11:10–12) after it.
The second-and-third-visit sentence is the edition's 12:14 note ('the third time I am ready to come'); the old English printed (2 Cor 13:4) after it. 13:4 heads its own note.
'from you' makes no sense in the sentence; read as ἡμῶν (a common vowel confusion). The guessed word is in brackets per the brief.

choices.english: you would be right to look for
choices.why: unreal apodosis without ἄν, as in late Greek; keeps Paul's irony in 11:4.

choices.english: the third part of the distance
choices.why: Severianus reads 'third heaven' as a third of the way up, since paradise is on earth.
'angel' keeps the stated metaphor from the angels who serve God.

bible_refs.note: dead to the law; joined to another, him who rose from the dead
